Header: Cassava Mosaic Virus Khate la chinangwa

Prevention: This viral disease is spread mainly through insected cuttings used as planting material and is also transmitted by whiteflies ( Bemisia tabaci ).
Planting material can look healthy but the disease can be present, so use plant certified disease-free cuttings from registered suppliers.
Sauti, Sagonja, komanso, Beatrice, Mkondezi,Maunjili,Silira,Yizaso, Phoso, Mulola, Mpale, CH06/033, CH05/143.
Avoid mixing planting materials i.e. certified and non-certified planting materials.
Sterilize tools used to prepare cuttings with fire or disinfectant such as sodium hypochrolite, 70% ethanol (Methylated spirit).
Practice crop rotation with maize or sweet potato every other growing season.
Remove weeds to discourage habitat for the vectors.
Intercrop with maize or cowpeas to repel whiteflies.
Avoid disease hotspot areas for seed production.
Monitoring: Check the cassava plants weekly for symptoms as soon as the plants start to sprout.
Look for yellow/white mottled spots on the leaves; wrinkled and deformed leaves; and the presence of small whiteflies on the leaves especially on the lower side of the leaf.
Also look for yellowing and very tiny leaves, tiny stems, stunted growth and small tubers.
Apply green direct controls as soon as disease symptoms are seen and yellow direct controls when whiteflies are present.
Direct Control: Uproot all infected plants once they are observed from the field/garden.
Dry and burn far from the field.

Restrictions: Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
Do not eat, drink or smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.
Do not apply insecticides in areas where cassava leaves are harvested for food.
